comment: Aliased operations whose behaviour is known to differ from the reference
somewhere, with the domain of the difference named.
This exists because `exact` was doing two jobs. It meant 'the reference
bytes are pinned', which is a statement about evidence, and it was being
read as 'this operation matches the reference everywhere', which is a
statement about behaviour. Those are different claims and an operation can
have the first without the second: every entry below is byte-pinned over
the inputs it covers and diverges outside them.
Each of these is already written out in prose on cyberchef-v11.3.0.md.
`section` names the heading anchor, and tools/ledger/generate.mjs refuses
an entry whose section is not there or whose alias is not registered, so
this file cannot outlive what it points at.
A resource limit is not a divergence. Every operation is bounded by the
execution budget, which the reference does not have at all; that is a
property of the runtime and is stated once under Limits.

divergences.domain: a capture group whose text occurs earlier in the match, and a failing section under `ignore_errors`
divergences.reason: the reference locates a capture group by searching the matched text for its characters rather than by its offset, and splices a failing section's error message into the output; the offset is used here, and a failing section contributes nothing exactly as a failing Fork branch does

divergences.domain: an odd number of hex digits, and text holding none
divergences.reason: the reference reads a trailing lone digit as a low nibble and decodes text with no digits to nothing; both are refused so a mistyped recipe complains instead of falling silent

divergences.domain: text the reference's bignum parser skips characters in
divergences.reason: the reference answers a number derived from the letters of `NaN`; reproducing it would mean reproducing that library's digit table for output nobody should act on

divergences.reason: the reference fills those bytes with `Math.random()`, so there is no output to match; refused exactly where it would have been unpredictable and accepted everywhere else

divergences.domain: a `Latin1` key holding a character above the byte range
divergences.reason: `crypto-api` packs four characters into a word with no mask, so a high character spills into the previous one's position; the digest is the HMAC of no key under any encoding

divergences.domain: regex mode with exotic Unicode property classes
divergences.reason: the portable automata engine is not XRegExp and has no lookaround; the simple and extended modes are unaffected
the reference's `{1,63}` per-label cap needs lookaround the portable engine does not have; it does not arise for real domains
